cohort: 259 facilities in 20 low- and middle-income countries, participating in both the WHO Global Survey on Maternal and Perinatal Health (2004-2008) and the WHO Multi-Country Survey on Maternal and Newborn Health (2010-2011)
finding: The study found no association between the increase in cesarean rate and the change of adverse outcome indexes, regardless of whether starting cesarean rates were already high or not.
